name: Society, Culture and Relationships
description: A contextual blueprint for communities, identity, relationships, family, marriage, norms, and lived experience.

guidance: Define the people, communities, relationships, institutions, place, period, and source perspectives represented.
Separate participant account, observed pattern, social norm, institutional rule, analyst interpretation, and causal claim.
Analyze identity, roles, power, norms, practices, relationships, conflict, change, and consequences in context.
Represent variation within groups and competing perspectives; do not treat one account or majority pattern as universal.
Attend to voice, positionality, sampling, translation, privacy, stigma, and whose perspective is absent.
Prefer thematic grids, perspective maps, and evidence trails; chart only comparable population or survey evidence with denominators.
Avoid deficit framing and unsupported generalization across cultures, genders, families, or communities.

sections.title: Social Context and Core Interpretation
sections.purpose: Define the people, relationships, and context represented, then answer the objective without erasing variation.

blocks.title: People, Context and Evidence Profile
instructions: Identify groups, relationships, institutions, geography, period, source perspectives, method, and absent voices where available.

blocks.title: Contextual Summary
instructions: Answer the objective through the central social pattern or tension, variation across perspectives, consequence, and evidence limitation.
Do not universalize one account, category, or cultural context.

blocks.title: Social and Relational Findings
instructions: Present distinct findings about identity, norm, role, power, relationship, practice, conflict, adaptation, change, or consequence with source perspective.

sections.title: Norms, Power and Relationship Dynamics
sections.purpose: Explain how social expectations, roles, resources, and institutions shape interaction and lived experience.

blocks.title: Dynamics and Context Analysis
instructions: Analyze norms, roles, power, resources, institutions, negotiation, conflict, care, belonging, and exclusion only where supported.
Distinguish participant meaning from analyst interpretation and pattern from causal mechanism.

blocks.title: Context-to-Experience Pathway
instructions: Map one supported pathway from norm or institution through interaction or resource condition to lived consequence; mark contested or missing links.

sections.title: Perspectives, Variation and Social Change
sections.purpose: Compare represented perspectives and explain where experiences converge, diverge, or change over time.

blocks.title: Variation and Change
instructions: Compare perspectives across relevant identities, generations, relationships, institutions, places, or periods while preserving within-group variation.
Do not explain difference through identity alone when structural or contextual evidence is absent.

blocks.title: Comparable Social Evidence

chart_slot.intent: Support one social claim with comparable population, survey, participation, distribution, or trend evidence.

fallback.message: No comparable quantitative social evidence is available.

instructions: Require compatible definitions, samples, denominators, periods, and groups; expose representation limits and avoid implying that frequency measures importance.

sections.title: Voices, Accounts and Evidence
sections.purpose: Make represented perspectives auditable and identify evidence-supported implications without speaking for absent groups.

blocks.title: Perspective and Evidence Trail
instructions: Tie findings to specific accounts, practices, patterns, institutional texts, observations, statistics, and source locations while identifying perspective.

blocks.title: Context-Sensitive Considerations
instructions: Frame implications as context-dependent considerations with affected groups, participation needs, risks, and ways to validate impact.
Avoid imposing a single cultural norm.

sections.title: Positionality, Missing Voices and Limits
sections.purpose: State how sampling, representation, context, method, and analyst position constrain the social interpretation.

blocks.title: Limitations and Absent Perspectives
instructions: Identify missing groups, self-selection, power in data collection, translation, privacy, stigma, geographic or historical specificity, source positionality, and causal limits only when material.
